translation: That is, wind-stroke, numbness, unfeeling hands and feet, consumption, fatigue, drum distension, hiccups, carbuncles, ulcers, sores, and scabies are diseases, and also accumulations. What the medical books call impediment (痹), rheum (飲), concretions (癥), and conglomerations (瘕) are all accumulations. The physiognomy book says: “Exposed teeth and protruding Adam’s apple, one starves to death in another province,” because the yangming is silted and accumulated and the lips are turned up and shortened; “If the root of the nose is broken, the flower fades early,” because the four sides of the bridge of the nose are congested and raised, forming a hollow shape.
